about: newhome 2026-11-17: each never-ported Revenge man's library moves, slot by slot (revlib.py rows_all.json's shape: {sid: {ids: {slot: ID}}}), as the installed folders play them with the library the game ships (content\movelib_revenge.bin, movelib2's build): movelib2's index plus movesteps' later-step entries. aki_import.py lays these over the index it is given. revlib.py today makes another library (see the private HANDOFF): this file keeps the shipped one's index until the library itself is rebuilt. The slots fixes2.no_struggle gives his own Revenge slam (on the Back Body Flip, @16250) are not listed: the importer makes them again, after this index. (2026-11-20, revmoves2) 14 slots play their library move on the No Mercy move its animations are made for, not the slot's reference move: Revenge's suplex pins (revenge:15ce_15cf German Suplex Pin 2850, revenge:15d8_15d9 2800, revenge:15e2_15e3 Tiger Suplex Pin 3030 -- each that move's pair frame for frame, ending in the bridge the pin's hold goes on from) were on 2610 Shin Breaker in slots 75 / 76, a move that doesn't go on to a pin, so both men snapped to standing out of the bridge. Revenge's turnbuckle dives with a cover (revenge:1bc5_1bc6 Ultimo Dragon 261 / 264, revenge:1be3_1be4 AKI Man / Han Zo Mon 264) stay on 12380, a dive at a lying man, as Revenge plays them there: its record gets the cover (toolsomimport rozenecords_damage.json: byte 0x22 = 0x22, flags 0x2020 -> 0x2220) so a hit square on the man goes on to the pin from the cover landing, and library_index.json's fifth role is the landing that follows the flight -- before, the cover landing was played as a plain landing and he snapped to standing. (2026-11-21, revmoves3) Dean Malenko's and Han Zo Mon's slot 22, revenge:1298_1299~142c -- No Mercy's move 1184 and its hold 1185 byte for byte, a hold (flags 0x2580) -- was on 16544, a move that goes on to a pin (16545, 0x300): the hold's animations played as a pin. It is played on 1184. And 19 slots the other way: a hold's or a pin's first step played on a move that ends -- revenge:1298_1299 (No Mercy's 1184, a hold) on 16574, revenge:1399_139b (No Mercy's 424, a pin: Wrath's 27 / 52 play it with its pin block on 964) on 16574 / 414 / 1024, revenge:129d_129f (No Mercy's 394, a pin) on 16574 (Scott Norton; British Bulldog's slot 62 keeps 414: no pin block in his Revenge list): the men dropped into the hold or the pin and the move ended, both getting up. They are played on 1184 / 424 / 394 (the lowest of the No Mercy moves with those animations byte for byte), whose holds and pins are the Revenge moves' own blocks byte for byte (gen\revanims.py rev_block in their lists). And (the user, 2026-11-21: 'whatever Revenge does') the moves Revenge goes on from, on No Mercy moves that end: 32 go on in Revenge to another move (their code's byte 15: code 155 = entry 183, a strike combo's next; 63 = 77; 196 = 236) -- played on the No Mercy move with their animations that goes on there (5612, 16312, 3372); 6 go on into a hold (a hold block whose loop starts where they end: 129c_129e, 14a4_14a5, 17e6_17e7) -- played on the No Mercy move with their animations whose hold is that block byte for byte (392, 512, 5672); 54 more (180c_180d, 17e2_17e3) sit in a strike's next step (entries 187-203), which No Mercy plays as a strike whatever the move's record (a test: Brickowski's 187 on 6852 played in the strike states and never went on, as on 5902; No Mercy's own twins sit in such steps too), so they keep their move. fixes2's no-struggle slams on 16250 stay as they are (by design).
